p: St Davids may be tiny, but the peninsula around it is packed with things to see and do. Pairing a visit to the Bug Farm with time on the coast is a great way to show children how the smallest creatures and the biggest landscapes are all part of the same picture.

The Bug Farm has also made a name for itself experimenting with insects as food, so if you've got a brave eater in the family, it's worth looking into what's on offer. Even if you don't fancy trying a cricket, it's a fascinating conversation starter about where our food might come from in future.

Close to the cathedral, the ruins of St Davids Bishop's Palace are atmospheric and fun to explore. St Non's Chapel, on the cliffs south of the city, marks the traditional birthplace of Saint David, and its holy well and coastal views make for a peaceful short walk. Boat trips to Ramsey Island run from St Justinian's in the season, offering the chance to spot seals, seabirds and sometimes porpoises.

Solva, a short drive east, is a pretty harbour village with colourful houses and a sheltered inlet, perfect for an ice cream and a stroll. Porthgain, to the north, has an old industrial harbour turned into a lovely little stop with galleries and a well-known seafood spot by the water. Between them, they make the perfect slow afternoon after a morning spent getting to know the bugs. The coast round here can be blowy even in summer, so bring an extra layer and sturdy shoes for the cliff paths.
